doc: The abstract, harness-agnostic entity registry — THE source the scaffolded core surface derives from. dadaia-workspace defines behaviors, personas, rules and skills agnostically; each harness receives an IMPLEMENTATION of them. A scaffolded core sub-agent without a Persona here, a core hook without a Deterministic Behavior here, or a core rule without an Abstract Rule here is forbidden (constitution, Anti-Slop Law, Derivation law). Operator-created entities are out of scope.

personas.mandate: Owner of the specs: backlog curation, SPEC authoring from the main thread's grill handoff, and product-memory reconciliation at closure; never dispatches.
Generic implementer: PLAN and TASKS as technical planning, production code and its tests, TDD-first, inside the task's declared write set.
The reviewer: three-axis review (standards, spec, bug surface) plus the six lenses — architecture, security, QA, product, audit, AI surface — at candidate close, before the PR; verdict-only.

behaviors.mandate: The workspace root holds only the sanctioned entries; any file-tool write that would mint a new top-level entry is blocked.

implementations.kimi-code: managed hook block in $KIMI_CODE_HOME/config.toml → the same Python gate

behaviors.mandate: Three path classes on every write: ADDITIVE always writable, PROTECTED blocked, MUTATING writable but scope-judged under repos/<slug>/ when the session is bound; no phase, no mode; every block carries one fix: line; races surfaced, never prevented.

implementations.claude: PreToolUse hook via dadaia_workspace.hooks.pre_gate (single merged entrypoint) + PostToolUse session heartbeat via dadaia_workspace.hooks.sdd_post_gate
implementations.codex: .codex/hooks.json PreToolUse wrapper → the same Python gate (pre + post)
implementations.kimi-code: managed hook block PreToolUse → the same Python gate (pre + post)

behaviors.mandate: The session's own bind selects which product memory is injected at prompt time; never another session's bind.

implementations.claude: UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart hooks via dadaia_workspace.hooks.ctx_inject; SessionStart also runs dadaia doctor --fix --expired-only --quiet (the reaper lane)
implementations.codex: SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit wrappers → dadaia_workspace.hooks.ctx_inject; SessionStart also runs the reaper lane
implementations.kimi-code: managed hook block → the same ctx_inject module
implementations.cursor: .cursor/hooks.json sessionStart only → dadaia_workspace.hooks.ctx_inject (additional_context): no prompt-time injection, a bind shows at the next session start; sessionStart also runs dadaia doctor --fix --expired-only --quiet (the reaper lane)
implementations.devin: .devin/hooks.v1.json UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart → dadaia_workspace.hooks.ctx_inject; SessionStart also runs the same reaper lane
implementations.copilot: .github/hooks/session-start.json sessionStart only → dadaia_workspace.hooks.ctx_inject (additionalContext): no prompt-time injection, a bind shows at the next session start; sessionStart also runs the same reaper lane

behaviors.mandate: Harness-independent: pre-push allows only work-branch pushes (the constitution's gitflow) and refuses integration/principal direct pushes (branch contract: `dd-gitflow-default`).

implementations.claude: .dadaia git hook (pre-push-ci-gate.sh) — identical for every harness

behaviors.mandate: tool caches land in absolute .dadaia/tmp/<tool>-cache (workspace_layout.tool_cache_env); a harness that cannot carry an env declares the gap, and a run there leaves an in-tree cache the doctor holds in reaped/ (fix: dadaia doctor --fix).

implementations.kimi-code: gap: no project-level env in the managed hook block

rules.mandate: AGENTS.md — the root map, the one always-on law file, projected read-only; scoped AGENTS.md files are the system of record per area; human-only in an instantiated workspace.

implementations.devin: AGENTS.md (native root + lazy on file access)

rules.mandate: Codex-native executable command policy (Starlark, the only rule dialect Codex executes): allows only the argv-closed readers ls and cat; every other command prompts or falls to the Codex default.

universal.doc: Harness-agnostic by construction — every supported harness reads these natively, so they need no per-harness derivation and no harness toggle.
